newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark targets upside as support holds.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark targets upside as support holds.

text.p: Dollar/mark is ready for a new probe of the upside as a key support level at 1.8050 held in jittery trading, analysts said on Monday.
Crucial for the dollar/mark rally will be a fundamental development, the Bundesbank's announcement on its repurchase agreements or repo rates on Tuesday, they added.
"That 1.8050 was important, just above the consolidation peak of July," said MCM CurrencyWatch analyst Scott Siller.
He was referring to the strong of 1.7995-to-1.8040 highs set in the week of July 14-19, before dollar/mark kicked off a July 31 rally that peaked with a near eight-year high.

Dollar/mark brushed 1.8050 overnight amid concern about global equities markets but recouped its gains along with the Dow Jones, hitting a session high of 1.8360 in late New York trading. Dollar/yen mirrored that action, dipping to 116.85 overnight only to end the day near a day's high of 108.08.

Siller also pointed out that the 1.8360 level was a significant resistance as "the 62-percent retracement of the uptrend from the (1.7456) low on July 10 to the 1.8913 high on August 6, in a nice, well defined upward channel."
While noting the dollar's healthy rebound, chartists said the next 24 hours may be trying for the U.S. unit.
The Bundesbank will announce its repo rate on Tuesday morning and the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market will announce its benchmark rates decision in mid-afternoon.
The market expects both the Bundesbank and the Fed to keep rates unchanged. The German repo rate is at 3.0 percent and the federal funds rate at 5.50 percent.
Chartists said the pivot for dollar/mark trading should be at 1.8250, and that the pair would probe either side all the way to 1.8050 or 1.85 in the event of a surprise.
Siller said closing "above 1.8280 marks, the previous low on August 13" was also an important rally signal.
That level triggered the surge to the recent high of 1.8665 marks -- another resistance level past the 1.85 hurdle.
Mark/yen may be instrumental if it corrects lower to the 64.20/25 area in a seven-day channel, said Siller who predicted "if we lose that, we'll go lower on that cross."
Dollar/yen remains in a broad 114.25-to-118.70 range -- from the low on August 8 to the high on August 15.

"If we convincgly get through 108.05, we'll see the high of Friday pretty quick," Siller forecast. "From there, we could get 119.58," the recent high on August 6, or even key psychological resistance at 121.00.
